subject: Clearpoint MAP: Acceptance thresholds, stop conditions & test owners
messages:
From: Eve Harrington <eve.h@clearpointhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alv@clearpointhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Evaluation acceptance criteria and MAP owners

Hi Priyom / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and clinical leads want a concise mutual action plan that calls out: exact success criteria we’ll test against, what constitutes a go/no‑go (stop conditions), and who on our side owns each acceptance test. We’re working to a hard internal cutover on Sept 3 and need the MAP in place this week so engineering can schedule integration tests.

Key asks from Clearpoint:
- A short list of acceptance thresholds (latency, accuracy/concordance, allowed hallucination rate, throughput).
- A test owner for each acceptance item (we’ll map to our QA contacts).
- Any hard stop/rollback triggers (e.g., >5% critical errors, P0 false positives).

Can you send a draft by EOD Wednesday PST? I’ve looped Tom (QA) for later pairing on test cases.

Thanks,
Eve
Eve Harrington
Sr. Program Manager, Clinical Ops
Clearpoint Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eve Harrington <eve.h@clearpointhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alv@clearpointhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance criteria and MAP owners

Eve — thanks for the clear ask. Draft below (high level) — Camila and I can populate a runbook and map owners. We’ll attach a spreadsheet with owners + acceptance tests by tomorrow.

Proposed acceptance thresholds (initial):
- Latency (tail): 95th percentile <= 220ms for single-turn inference (50 token prompt).
- Throughput: sustained 60 concurrent requests with median latency < 120ms.
- Concordance / accuracy: 85%+ on curated clinical prompt set (see sample prompts).
- Hallucination / safety: <1% rate for high‑severity hallucinations (cases flagged by our safety model).
- Error budget / reliability: <0.5% 5xx over the evaluation window.

Stop conditions (go/no‑go triggers):
- Any single-day critical safety failure affecting production metrics >0.5% (manual hold).
- Regressions: any 5‑point drop in concordance vs baseline on the same prompt set during canary.
- Persistent latency regressions (95th percentile > 450ms for >2 hours).

Immediate next steps:
1) Camila to attach runbook + owner mapping (tomorrow).
2) Clearpoint to confirm who will own each acceptance test on their side (Tom/QA).
3) We’ll schedule smoke tests and a 48‑hour canary the week of Aug 24.

If that reads OK I’ll compile into a single MAP doc and include a DocuSign-ready acceptance checklist for signatures.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Eve Harrington <eve.h@clearpointhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alv@clearpointhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 14:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance criteria and MAP owners

On Tue, Aug 18, 2026 at 09:05, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Proposed acceptance thresholds (initial):

Adding a runbook sketch and owner assignments. Attached: acceptance-tests-runbook.md (runs through smoke, integration, load, and safety test cases). Highlights:

- Smoke tests (owner: Clearpoint QA / Tom Alvarez): basic prompt/response sanity, top‑k correctness on 50 core prompts. Pass = 90% matching on expected response family.
- Integration tests (owner: Clearpoint Eng): API auth, rate‑limit handling, key rotation, end‑to‑end logging. Pass = no auth failures over 100 requests.
- Load tests (owner: Redwood infra — Camila): 60–120 concurrent clients in 30‑minute windows, monitor 95th percentile latency and GPU UTIL. Pass = 95p <= 220ms.
- Safety regressions (owner: Redwood safety — Marissa): run safety classifier against 1,000 probe prompts. Pass = high‑severity flags <1%.

Notes on measurement: we’ll provide the exact prompt sets and a small harness to run locally or from Clearpoint CI. I’ve also put basic input formatting checks as a precondition.

Attaching runbook (stub) and will fold owners into the spreadsheet.

Camila

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Eve Harrington <eve.h@clearpointhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance criteria and MAP owners

Quick operational notes:
- SLA / fallback: Agree we need a fallback plan. Propose: if canary shows >30% latency regression vs baseline for >1 hour, we automatically switch routing to a lower‑latency model variant (same API surface) and open a P1 with both teams.
- Cost/quantization: If Clearpoint wants 8‑bit quantized variants to reduce cost, we should add a quality delta acceptance (e.g., <3% drop in concordance) before allowing quantized model in canary.
- Telemetry: we’ll provide a tokenized cost estimate for the evaluation window so procurement can see projected spend.

If that’s acceptable I’ll include the fallback wording in the MAP spreadsheet.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eve Harrington <eve.h@clearpointhealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alv@clearpointhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:09:00 +0000
Subject: MAP v1.3 and proposed close timeline

Hi all — attached is MAP_v1.3.xlsx (owners tab + acceptance checklist). Summary timeline (proposed):
- Aug 25: Clearpoint to confirm owner names for each test.
- Aug 26–27: Redwood provides harness + sample prompt sets; Clearpoint runs smoke tests.
- Aug 30–31: Integration + load tests (48h canary window).
- Sept 1: Safety sweep and final reconciliation.
- Sept 3: Executive signoff window (target close).

Procurement note: I added a DocuSign checklist and a short SLO appendix (see slo_sample.pdf). For signatures we’ll need the legal contact (name + email) — Eve, can you share that contact and confirm approval authority?

Attachments: MAP_v1.3.xlsx (spreadsheet); slo_sample.pdf; acceptance-tests-runbook.md

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Eve Harrington <eve.h@clearpointhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alv@clearpointhealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 23:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MAP v1.3 and proposed close timeline

Thanks — the MAP looks good and the timeline is workable. A couple quick items:
- Our legal contact for signatures is Sandra Liu (sandra.liu@clearpointhealth.com). She’ll be the signatory on the DocuSign.
- We’ll take ownership of the smoke and integration tests (Tom will lead).
- We want one minor change: raise the concordance threshold to 87% for the clinical prompt set (we’ll accept that as passive gating for the first canary and make it hard gate for final signoff).

Please update the spreadsheet and send the DocuSign package; Tom and I will validate the runbook this week and confirm owners by EOD Aug 25.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Eve
Eve Harrington
Sr. Program Manager, Clinical Ops
Clearpoint Health
